chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Joining the Mills Blue Rhythm Band under Carroll Dickerson
summary: Holmes joined soon after the band went into the Cotton Club, replacing Jobetus McCord; he recalls Dickerson, Hayes Alvis and Crawford Wethington.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Did you join that band then? You were at the Lafayette?
Not then, no.
No.
No. No, I wasn't in the theatre then. That's the first time I heard of it. They were so successful, Mills booked them right into the Cotton Club, and he sent Cab Calloway on the road.
And that's when you joined again.

Well, soon after that. I don't remember whether it was the first week or not. I think they were in the club when I went in, you know, for a few days or something like that, when I joined the band. That's when Carroll Dickerson was made the leader; he was put in front of the band...
That's when Mills called the band Earl Jackson...
And his Rhythm Band.
...and His Rhythm Band. Now, do you remember, then, who the personnel were?
Holmes (10/11) - 7
No.

Because I have a picture here of the Blue Rhythm Band, which is quite early. And it has Carroll Dickerson fronting the band. But at this point, now, when you came in with the Blue Rhythm Band, the pianist was Edgar Hayes.
Okay. There's Carroll Dickerson. That's Willie Lynch on drums. That's Briggs.
Pete Briggs, right?
Right.
Now, was Pete Briggs there when you were there?
No.
Or was it Elmer James? Or Hayes.
Hayes Alvis.
It was Hayes Alvis
I think Hayes and the leader went in together. Carroll Dickerson...
I see. Carroll Dickerson and Hayes Alvis came together.
I mean, he came to New York with Carroll.
Who were the other saxes, then, when you were there? Was Crawford Webbington there?
Yup.
So you and Crawford were the two altos?
And Cass McCord.
Holmes (10/11) - 8
And you replaced Cass McCord's brother, Jobetus.
Jobetus. Yeah, I replaced him.
So therefore, you and Hayes probably came in at about the same time.
Yeah, around the same time.
Because Jobetus and Pete Briggs must have left together.
Around the same time. Carroll Dickerson had just come from Chicago, you know. And I know what'cha' callit came with Carroll... I didn't know Gus Aikins was in this band. Gus been in all the bands.
